title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is assigning to every conformal surface X (possibly non-orientable, without boundary) a canonical Riemannian metric Q_X compatible with the conformal structure and natural under all conformal automorphisms. The previous page summarizes the result. Q_X exists except in two cases. (a) X ≅ C: only a homothety class of invariant flat metrics exists. (b) X ≅ P^1_C: no Aut-invariant metric exists. Instead there is the set R(X) of normalized round metrics of area 1, a single G-orbit and a 3-dimensional homogeneous space, in modern terms PSL2(C)/SO(3) ≅ H^3. For a subgroup H, an H-invariant Q in R(X) exists iff H is relatively compact, and it is unique iff X^H = ∅.

This page continues in three steps.

1. Bracketed NB on the non-connected case. The equivariant statement should be adapted: H stabilizes one component and permutes the others. H is assumed finite, and the condition X^H = ∅ is restated for the fixed component (no points of that component fixed by all of H).

2. Curvature dichotomy, wherever Q_X is defined.
- Q_X has negative curvature iff X is hyperbolic (universal cover a disc), and then Q_X has constant curvature -1. This is the Poincaré metric.
- Q_X is flat iff the universal cover of X is C. This includes case (a), where Q_X is unique only up to a constant, and covers C, C*, tori, and the non-orientable quotients (Klein bottle, open Möbius band).
- The only remaining case is the real projective plane, X = P^1/(antipodal map). There Q_X is the homogeneous metric of constant positive curvature, invariant under its compact conformal group SO(3).
- Conclusion: whenever Q_X is defined it has constant curvature.

3. Equivariant extension. The same holds for Q_{X,H} when X ≅ P^1 and H ⊂ Aut_conf(X) is finite with X^H = ∅. The unique H-invariant normalized round metric has constant curvature > 0, determined up to homothety.
- Geometric meaning: H compact acts on R(X) ≅ H^3 with totally geodesic fixed set Fix(H), whose boundary at infinity is X^H.
- If X^H = ∅, Fix(H) is a single point. Examples: dihedral, tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral subgroups of SO(3), or groups containing the antipodal map.
- If X^H ≠ ∅ (cyclic groups, reflections), Fix(H) is a geodesic or a plane, so uniqueness fails.

Margin note: on the space Riem(X) of all Riemannian metrics, the Aut_conf(X)-action reduces in cases (a) and (b). In case (b) the relevant space is the 3-dimensional R(X); any two distinct Q, Q' in R(X) are non-proportional. He floats a 'notion of distinguished Riemannian metric', presumably also for the discontinuous (discrete group) case. Purpose: rigid, functorial geometric normalizations for the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' program; the next page treats bordered surfaces via the orientation double cover with anti-involution.
errors: Minor imprecision: 'Q_X hyperbolique (i.e. à courbure <0)' conflates negative curvature with the constant -1 normalization. Harmless, since he then states curvature is constant -1.

In the flat non-compact cases (C*, cylinder-type quotients) the normalization fixing Q_X (rather than its homothety class) is not specified on this page. For tori, area 1 works; for C* some length normalization would be needed.
'X^H = ∅' must be read as no common fixed point of all of H, not as fixed-point-freeness of each element. Only the former is consistent with non-cyclic subgroups of SO(3) giving uniqueness.

ideas.what: Canonical constant-curvature metric in the conformal class of any (possibly non-orientable) Riemann surface: curvature -1 if hyperbolic, flat if the universal cover is C, positive in the RP^2 case
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization theorem / Poincaré metric, extended to Klein surfaces

ideas.what: Normalized round metrics on P^1 form a 3-dimensional homogeneous space (≅ H^3); a compact H gives a unique invariant one iff H has no common fixed point on P^1
ideas.modern_name: Fixed points of compact groups acting on hyperbolic 3-space; ideal boundary of the fixed set

ideas.what: H-equivariant canonical spherical metric for finite H ⊂ Aut(P^1) with X^H = ∅, i.e. a canonical spherical orbifold metric on P^1/H
Idea of a functorial 'distinguished Riemannian metric' attached to a conformal surface, also in the presence of group actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Douady–Earle (1986) for conformally natural barycentric extension

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but classical recapitulation of uniformization: constant curvature -1, 0 or +1 (the last only for RP^2), plus the standard fact that a compact group acting on H^3 fixes a single point iff it has no common fixed point at infinity. It is a nice functorial organization (equivariant, non-orientable, non-connected), but nothing here goes beyond known results.
transcription_corrections: 'à courbure <0' and 'de courbure constante égale à -1': 'constante' is an insertion above the line.
'[y inclus le cas a) ci-dessus, où on a encore une Q_X unique à cte]' is a reasonable reading.
'Le cas [-restant-] est celui du plan projectif réel': 'restant' is struck through, and the line likely continues 'où, toutefois, ... Q_X est une métrique homogène, de courbure cte et > 0'.
Final line likely reads '... X^H = ∅, à homothétie près ... quelconques, de courbure constante > 0' (bottom line partly illegible).
Margin: 'o-connexe' likely 'non connexe' or '0-connexe'. The 'dans les cas a), b) de 4)' reference likely points to the cases of page 12).
Margin: 'quelles que soient Q, Q' ∈ R(X), Q ≠ Q' ⇒ Q et Q' non proportionnelles'.
